To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
interleukin- 1 suppresses mesengial cell growth and calcium entry.
the growth of cultured rat mesangial (renal glomerular) cells is suppressed by interleukin- 1 (IL- 1), and this suppression is associated with inhibition of extracellular calcium entry to the cells.
the growth of mesangiocytes in culture is suppressed by interleukin- 1 and the calcium channel blocker nicardipine.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of IL-1 in the regulation of cell growth of rat mesangium in vitro.
the mechanism of the growth inhibition by IL-1 in rat mesangial cell.
the mechanism of action of IL-1 on mesangial cell proliferation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
IL-1 inhibits mesangial cell proliferation by suppressing Ca2+ entry through inhibition of Ca2+-permeable channels.
the inhibition of mesangial cell proliferation by IL-1 is mediated by a mechanism that involves inhibition of Ca2+-entry into the cells.
IL-1 inhibits the proliferation of mesangial cell via inhibition of Ca(2+)-entry.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IL-1 may suppress mesangial cell hyperplasia via inhibition of Ca(2+)-dependent cell cycle progression.
IL-1 inhibits cell growth via the suppression of the extracellular Ca2+-dependent signal pathway.
IL-1 inhibits the growth of mesanglial cells by suppressing the influx of Ca2+ into the cell.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IL-1 may play an important role in regulating mesangial cell proliferation and mesangial cell hypertrophy in the glomerulus.
IL-1 may be an important regulator of mesangial cell function in vivo, particularly in the setting of glomerular injury.
IL-1 inhibits mesangial cell proliferation by inhibiting Ca2+ entry, and the mechanism of IL-1 inhibition may be through inhibition of Ca2+/calmodulin-dependent protein kinase II.
